title: How the browser picks the cookies for one request
purpose: Apply the Domain, Path, Secure and SameSite checks to decide which stored cookies one request carries.
sequence_reason: A cookie travels only when every check passes, so the learner follows one cookie jar through the checks for different requests.
summary: A browser stores five cookies from shop.example.com. For each request it checks Domain (which hosts), Path (which URL paths), Secure (https only) and SameSite (Strict, Lax or None against same-site and cross-site requests). HttpOnly hides a cookie from page scripts but the cookie is still sent. The __Secure- and __Host- name prefixes force safe attributes.
explanation: A request carries a stored cookie only when the host matches Domain, the path matches Path, the scheme satisfies Secure, and SameSite allows the request context. HttpOnly changes what JavaScript can read, not what the request carries.

learning_check.question: A form on another site sends a POST to shop.example.com. Which SameSite value lets the cookie go with it?
learning_check.answer: Only SameSite=None (with Secure). Strict never goes cross-site, and Lax goes cross-site only on a top-level navigation with a safe method such as GET, and POST is not safe.

scenes.heading: Which cookies go with this request?
scenes.narration: The browser stores cookies. Before each request, it checks every stored cookie and sends only the cookies that pass.

scenes.heading: Five cookies from shop.example.com
scenes.narration: Here are five cookies from shop.example.com. Each line shows the attributes that the Set-Cookie header gave the cookie.

scenes.heading: Domain and Path pick the URL
scenes.narration: Without Domain, a cookie goes only to the host that set it. With Domain, subdomains get it too. Path=/account matches /account and its subpaths.

left.label: Domain
items: Never a public suffix like com

visual.verdict: Path is not a security boundary

scenes.heading: Secure and HttpOnly do different jobs
scenes.narration: Secure sends the cookie only over https. HttpOnly hides the cookie from page scripts, but their requests still carry it.

visual.verdict: HttpOnly controls JavaScript, not the request

scenes.heading: SameSite looks at where the request starts
scenes.narration: A site is the scheme plus the registrable domain. Strict stays same-site. Lax also allows cross-site top-level GET navigations. None allows every request and needs Secure.

items: Lax: plus cross-site top-level navigation with GET

scenes.heading: A link from another site
scenes.narration: A link on news.other.org opens shop.example.com. The Strict cart cookie stays home. Lax and None cookies go with the GET navigation.

path.label: Sends __Host-sid, widget, theme; cart and prefs stay

scenes.heading: A cross-site form POST
scenes.narration: Now a form on other.org sends a POST. POST is not a safe method, so Lax cookies stay home. Only the None cookie goes.

scenes.heading: Name prefixes force safe attributes
scenes.narration: The browser rejects a __Secure- cookie without Secure. A __Host- cookie also needs Path=/ and no Domain, so only its own host gets it.

visual.verdict: __Host- treats the origin as the boundary
